what_it_does: This paper presents a specialized 64-kilobit memory module that performs mathematical operations directly inside the memory—a technique called compute-in-memory (CIM). The chip blends analog computation (fast but lower precision) with digital computation (slower but exact), intelligently switching between them depending on how much accuracy each part of the calculation needs. It includes a dedicated sign-bit processor to handle the mathematical sign (positive/negative), and a smart quantizer that dynamically adjusts precision allocation between analog and digital portions, conserving energy when precision requirements drop.
